outline.chapter_title: Foundations of Large Language Models and Their Context Windows
outline.description: Introduces modern transformer based large language models, defines the concept of a context window, presents typical sizes used in popular models such as LLaMA2 or GPT4, explains how limited context harms downstream tasks and motivates the need for much longer windows.
subtopics: Definition and role of the context window
Typical context sizes in public models
Impact of limited context on applications
Motivation for extending beyond standard limits

outline.description: Explains why transformers require explicit position information, reviews absolute learned embeddings, sinusoidal encodings, relative position mechanisms and prepares the reader for rotational techniques.

outline.chapter_title: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE): Theory and Mechanics
outline.description: Provides a deep dive into Rotary Position Embedding used by many state-of-the-art LLMs. Derives the mathematical formulation from complex multiplication perspective, explains frequency scaling via base theta=10000 and shows how RoPE integrates with query-key attention.

outline.chapter_title: Challenges When Extending the Context Window
outline.description: Discusses three major obstacles identified when trying to increase an LLM's effective length: catastrophic values introduced by unseen positions, scarcity/lack-of-long-text data sets and computational cost together with attention dispersion over millions tokens.
subtopics: "Distribution shift" between trained and extended positions
"Attention density dilution" across very long sequences
